AUTHOR: Chicchon, M; Bedon, H; Del-Blanco, CR; Sipiran, I
TITLE: Semantic Segmentation of Fish and Underwater Environments Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks and Learned Active Contours
REGION: Mixed: SUIM (global), DeepFish (tropical Australia), RockFish, own drone footage from beaches and fish farms in Peru
SPECIES: Fish (vs water background, seafloor/obstacle) - pixel classes
DATA: New relabeled dataset of 1824 images: SUIM 918, DeepFish 150, RockFish 280, own underwater-drone video frames >200, plus internet images
V_EV: Sec. IV-C: 'an image captured in a fish farm with many fish and suspended particles close to the drone camera, where the U-Net model obtains a better result'
D_EV: Sec. III-A: 'All the images were resized at 256 x 320 pixels and divided into three subsets with 1280/272/272 images for the training/validation/testing'
R_EV: Sec. IV-C: 'calculated on the basis of the average of the results of each image in the test split' (single pooled dataset; no external test)
E_EV: Sec. VI: 'Combining U-Net-scSE with a pre-trained EfficientNet-B0 lightweight architecture gives a value of 86% mIoU and 26.61 mm of mHD95' (segmentation metrics only)
ARCH: U-Net-scSE and DeepLabV3+ with MobileNetV2/EfficientNet/ResNeSt encoders; combined CE+Dice+Chan-Vese active-contour loss
NOTE: INCL borderline: test set pools SUIM (benchmark/internet compilation) with field-deployment imagery (DeepFish, RockFish ROV, own underwater-drone footage incl. fish farms); not benchmark-only, so INCL=Y, but results are not reported separately for field imagery (only qualitative per-source examples). Split given only as image counts; part of images are video frames -> 이미지/프레임 무작위 (alternatively NR). No detection threshold; segmentation so C_ALL=NR not NA.
